labels.label: prop:mesure_admissible
labels.notes: Unmarked and partial, which is right: the proposition is about every strongly causal E>=0-manifold and this file proves the model half at M = E_kappa, kappa > 0. The ledger regex (tools/ledger.py:247) finds no mark anywhere in the file. Line 531's '**`prop:mesure_admissible`'s conclusion...**' does not match the regex and lies past the 4000-character window. The label is cited in the first 4000 characters. (1) modelMeasures is an honest instance of Causal.Causality.ModelMeasures (Causal/SingularGeroch.lean:174). The structure asks, at each p, for an open U containing p, causally convex in the top open set, with an AdmissiblePastOn / AdmissibleFutureOn measure. The file takes U = top, as E0.modelMeasures and timelikeLine_modelMeasures do, with the finite muE kappa transported by admissiblePastOn_top / admissibleFutureOn_top. It is not vacuous: muE is AdmissiblePast and AdmissibleFuture on all of E_kappa. The paper's relative compactness of U_p only buys finiteness, and ModelMeasures asks for finiteness directly. (2) mesure_admissible has the type '(exists mu, (massive kappa).AdmissiblePast mu) and exists mu, (massive kappa).AdmissibleFuture mu' under [Fact (0 < kappa)] only. This is exactly the conclusion of SingularFlatAxioms.mesure_admissible at C = massive kappa (checked with #check), with nothing extra. Unlike E0.mesure_admissible, it is proved directly from admissible_muE, not by instantiating the strict theorem: the strict library has no SingularFlatAxioms witness at E_kappa (grep; that is T-ett-singular-sfa). So it does not exercise the abstract theorem at E_kappa, and the ledger must not say 'through SingularFlatAxioms.mesure_admissible'. (3) Read literally against l.1736-1737: lam3_past and lam3_future give Regular, property 3 and property 4. They match the AdmissiblePast / AdmissibleFuture fields (Causal/Measure.lean:93-114) one for one, with p <= q, p != q for p < q and outer measure for property 4 (rem:mesure_bord). Property 2 is left out, as the paper leaves it out on the model. Its failure is lam3_univ. 'Borel' holds: MeasurableSpace (Cone kappa) is definitionally borel (rfl), and BorelSpace (Massive kappa) is Prod.borelSpace, Cone being second countable by secondCountable_of_proper (#synth). (4) paper_measures_local is at least the paper's local form, l.1734-1743. In every neighbourhood N of every p there is an open U with p in U, U inside N, closure of U compact, U causally convex in E_kappa, and lam3 restricted to U admissible on U in the past and in the future. The chart clause is trivial at the model. modelMeasures_local is the same statement with the measures made existential. (5) Static layer. static_mesure_dieckmann_of is minkowski_mesure_dieckmann_of (Causal/MinkowskiMeasure.lean:69) with minkowski n replaced by staticCausality X, line for line. static_exists_isOpen_subset_J*_diff_inter / static_pos_*_inter are proved this way: J^-(p) is closed, q is not in J^-(p) (causality), and q is in the closure of I^-(q), so I^-(q) meets the complement of J^-(p) intersected with W in a non-empty open set. This is the E_kappa analogue of E0.pos_*_inter, with no axis-segment hypothesis because there is no BTZ line. static_frontier_section_subsingleton_of_* is correct for any <<-past/future set, open or not: dist(y.2,x) < y.1 - t gives (t,x) << y, and I^-(y) is open and contained in P, so (t,x) is in the interior of P. Fubini (prod_apply_symm) then makes the frontier null for dt (x) nu, nu s-finite. static_admissible_of_equiv and static_admissible*On_restrict_of mirror E0.admissible*_of_equiv and E0.admissible*On_restrict_of (Causal/Port/MeasuresE0.lean:567, 576, 713, 742): property 4 through restriction_convexe, property 3 through the local form (kb/0148). (6) The measure-theoretic core was read and kernel-checked. coneMeasure is polar_*((dr restricted to ]0,oo[) (x) Haar of AddCircle kappa). coneMeasure_pos: a ball about mk p contains polar(p.r + eps/2, p.theta), with r > 0, so the preimage is a non-empty open subset of {r > 0}. coneMeasure_closedBall bounds the mass by R*kappa, which makes it finite on compacts. The apex is null. polar_surjective follows from polar_rad_theta and mk_surjective. lam3Riem_equiv holds because the density r is positive a.e. on ]0,oo[, and absolute continuity passes through prod and map. (7) Finding 4 is correct. polar sends {u <= 0} to the apex (ConePoint.of u theta = <max u 0, theta>), so any m positive on opens gives the apex mass at least m(]-oo,0[)*kappa > 0 (map_polar_apex_pos). Its product with dt charges R x {apex}, which lam3 does not, so it is not << lam3. It is nevertheless admissible both ways (exists_admissible_charging_singLine, through static_admissible_of_equiv with nu = polar_*(dr (x) dtheta) over all of R, open-pos by Continuous.isOpenPosMeasure_map, OpenPos.lean:145). Both muE and this measure are admissible, so admissibility does not determine the null-set class: the conclusion is fair. It concerns the roadmap (the target title 'in the class of lambda_3' and the planner's step (3)), not the paper, which never claims an admissible measure lies in lambda_3's class. (8) Finding 2 is correct and a confirmation, not an error. A finite measure is admissible both ways at E_kappa, where the singular line is timelike and there is no BTZ point, so rem:mesure_unilaterale's hypothesis 'as soon as the spacetime carries a BTZ line' cannot be dropped. The paper's own rem:mesure_unilaterale_ptr says this. Minkowski (E_{2pi}, minkowski_mesure_dieckmann) already witnessed that the hypothesis is sharp. The new content is that a non-empty massive singular line is no obstruction. The REPORT's 'the pair mu_-, mu_+ of l.1727 is forced only by E_0' overreaches: it is proved at the models only, not for every E_{>0}-manifold. (9) The question, which lambda_3 on E_kappa, is harmless and needs no OQ (no OQ-87), as at E_0. The candidate readings all have the same null sets, are all locally finite and all charge open sets. They are dt dr dtheta (lam3), the Riemannian dt (x) r dr dtheta (lam3Riem, which is Lebesgue measure of R^3 at kappa = 2pi through coneTwoPiIsoEuclidean), and the chart pull-back (2pi/kappa) dt (x) r dr dtheta (computed by hand, correct). admissible_of_equiv, admissible_of_equiv_riem and admissible*On_restrict_of cover every finite or restricted version. What is not formalized is properties 1, 3, 4 for the infinite lam3Riem itself, which needs IsLocallyFiniteMeasure (coneArea kappa). It is trivially true; see the minor finding.

findings.what: Routing. Findings 1 (l.1736-1737 holds as printed) and 2 (one measure both ways, so rem:mesure_unilaterale's BTZ hypothesis is needed) are confirmations, not errors in the paper. Finding 4 (the planner's polar image of a Gaussian over all of R charges the apex) is about the roadmap target title and route only. If any of them enters paper_findings, it would reach the author as a defect of the paper. Finding 3 (l.1742-1743) is the existing paper finding of T-ett-measures-e0, already in the row's paper_findings, extended to E_kappa.
findings.fix: Do not add paper_findings entries for findings 1, 2, 4: put 1 and 2 in scope_notes, and 4 in the roadmap journal / scope_notes as a roadmap note. For finding 3, extend the existing paper_findings sentence rather than duplicating it, by appending: 'At E_kappa, kappa > 0, the local form holds for every measure positive on non-empty open sets (Causal.MeasuresEAlpha.static_pos_past_inter, static_pos_future_inter).'

findings.what: Overreach in wording: 'it confirms that the pair mu_-, mu_+ of l.1727 is forced only by E_0' is proved only at the models E_kappa, not for every E_{>0}-manifold. Minkowski (E_{2pi}, Causal.minkowski_mesure_dieckmann) already showed that the BTZ hypothesis of rem:mesure_unilaterale is needed. What is new is that a non-empty massive (timelike) singular line is no obstruction.
findings.fix: Record as: 'At E_kappa, kappa > 0, a model whose singular line is timelike and non-empty, one finite measure is admissible in the past and in the future (Causal.MeasuresEAlpha.exists_admissible_past_future): a massive singular line is no obstruction, consistent with rem:mesure_unilaterale and rem:mesure_unilaterale_ptr, which restrict the obstruction to BTZ lines.'

findings.what: The row '`μ₋`, `μ₊` (l.1727) | ⚠ weakened (stronger conclusion)' mislabels by kb/0006, where ⚠ weakened means the Lean theorem assumes less. A stronger conclusion is a carried item.
findings.fix: At graduation: '| `μ₋`, `μ₊` (l.1727) | ✓ carried, stronger: one finite measure for both (`exists_admissible_past_future`) |'. Do the same in the ledger's hypothesis summary.

findings.what: Reading of lambda_3. The primary reading lam3 = dt (x) dr dtheta is not Lebesgue measure of R^3 even at kappa = 2pi, which is dt (x) r dr dtheta. Properties 1, 3, 4 are proved for the infinite lam3 only. For the Riemannian lam3Riem only the finite-class lemma (admissible_of_equiv_riem) and the null-set equivalence are proved. This is disclosed (SCOPE (c), the REPORT's question) and harmless: same null sets, both locally finite. No OQ is needed.
findings.fix: Optional, at graduation or later: add IsLocallyFiniteMeasure (coneArea kappa) and lam3Riem_past / lam3Riem_future, or one lemma 'every locally finite measure with the null sets of lam3 satisfies properties 1, 3, 4 in both senses'. Otherwise record the reading as settled by the class result, as at E_0.

graduation.curation_text_prop_mesure_admissible: T-ett-measures-ealpha (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (routing of findings, a checklist label, stale blocked_on; fixed at graduation), Causal/Model/MeasuresEAlpha.lean: the measures of the proof at E_κ, κ > 0 (massive κ = staticCausality (Cone κ)). The sentence l.1736-1737 as printed, λ₃ read as dt ⊗ dr dθ in the cylindrical coordinates (MeasuresEAlpha.lam3): λ₃ satisfies properties 1., 3., 4. in the past (lam3_past) and in the future (lam3_future). It is infinite (lam3_univ), hence the restriction to a relatively compact U_p (l.1741), where λ₃ restricted is admissible on both sides (lam3_admissibleOn; paper_measures_local: such a U_p in every neighbourhood of every point). One finite measure, muE κ = (lam3 κ).toFinite, is admissible in the past and in the future at once (exists_admissible_past_future). Hence MeasuresEAlpha.modelMeasures (U = E_κ, as E0.modelMeasures) and MeasuresEAlpha.mesure_admissible, the proposition's conclusion at E_κ, proved directly: E_κ has no SingularFlatAxioms witness yet (T-ett-singular-sfa). Static layer, for every static ℝ × X: Minkowski's reduction verbatim (static_mesure_dieckmann_of); null frontiers of every ≪-past or ≪-future set for dt ⊗ ν, ν any s-finite measure (static_prod_frontier_of_past, _of_future, by vertical sections); the class result and restriction to causally convex open sets (static_admissible_of_equiv, static_admissiblePastOn_restrict_of, static_admissibleFutureOn_restrict_of); property 3's local form (static_pos_past_inter, static_pos_future_inter; kb/0148). Hypotheses: every E≥0-manifold → strengthened (M = E_κ); strong causality → used only in its open form by paper_measures_local (massive_stronglyCausalOpen); μ₋, μ₊ → carried, stronger (one measure for both). A massive singular line is no obstruction to admissibility in both senses, consistent with rem:mesure_unilaterale, whose obstruction needs a BTZ line. The reading of λ₃ on E_κ (no Cartesian coordinates for κ ≠ 2π) is settled by the class result, as at E₀. dt dr dθ, the Riemannian dt ⊗ r dr dθ (lam3Riem_equiv) and the chart pull-back (2π/κ) dt ⊗ r dr dθ have the same null sets. Every finite measure in that class is admissible on both sides (admissible_of_equiv, admissible_of_equiv_riem), as is every restriction to a causally convex open set (admissiblePastOn_restrict_of, admissibleFutureOn_restrict_of); no OQ. Roadmap note, not a paper finding: the planner's polar image of a measure on all of ℝ × ℝ/κℤ charges the apex (map_polar_apex_pos), so its product with dt is not in the class of λ₃ (not_absolutelyContinuous_map_polar). It is admissible nonetheless (exists_admissible_charging_singLine): properties 1.-4. do not determine the null-set class.
